title: Why cutting onions makes eyes water
answer: Cutting onion cells releases a volatile sulfur compound called syn-propanethial-S-oxide. It reaches the moist surface of the eye and irritates it, which triggers tears. A sharp knife and a slower cut can reduce the spray; chilling the onion may also slow the reaction.

title: Descaling an electric kettle
answer: Descaling directions differ by kettle model, so follow its manual. For the KRUPS Control Line model, the manufacturer describes either 0.5 L of 8° white vinegar left unheated for 1 hour, or 0.5 L of boiled water with 25 g citric acid left for 15 minutes; then empty and rinse 5–6 times. Do not assume these amounts apply to another model.

followups.duration: The KRUPS instructions give two durations: 1 hour for the unheated vinegar method, or 15 minutes after adding citric acid to boiled water. Those directions are model-specific.

title: Safe cooking temperature for egg dishes
answer: For casseroles and other dishes containing eggs, USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service guidance says to cook to at least 160°F (71°C), checked with a food thermometer. Cooking time for a boiled egg depends on size and method; this source does not establish a universal timing.
